div.head: V Atr 29
div.ab: ⁊ gyf ænig amánsumad man, butan hit friðbena sy, on þæs cynges neaweste ahwar gewunige, ær ðam þe he hæbbe godcunde bote georne gebogene, þonne plihte he him sylfum ⁊ eallan his æhtan.
⁊ gif ænig amánsumad man, butan hit friðbena sy, on þæs cynges neaweste ahwar gewunige, ær þam þe he hæbbe godcunde bote georne gebogene, þonne plihte he him sylfum ⁊ eallan his æhtan.
⁊ gif ænig amánsumad man, buton hit friðbena sy, on ðæs cynincges neawiste ahwar gewunige, ær ðam þe he hæbbe godcunde bote georne gebogene, þonne plihte he to him silfum oððe to his æhtan.

And if any excommunicated man, unless it be one who is a suppliant for protection, remains anywhere near the king, before he has readily submitted to the amends required by the church, it shall be at the risk of [losing] his life or his possessions.

Und wenn ein excommunicirter Mensch — ausser wenn es ein Asyl-Erbitter ist —, bevor er willig sich geistlicher Busse unterzogen hat, irgendwo in des Königs Umgebung bleibt, dann bringe er Verwirkungsgefahr seinem Leben und (oder D) all seiner Habe.

And if an excommunicated person — unless he is a suppliant for protection — remains anywhere in the king's presence before he has willingly submitted to ecclesiastical penance, then let him put at risk his life and (or, D) all his possessions.
div.note: Liebermann compares I Em 3; II Em 4.
